name: Religions trivia (hard)
description: 50 hard questions about the world's religions, large and small: beliefs, practices, holidays, history; respectful, no claims about which is true. Written by Claude from cited web pages; every question names its page. Checked by a second model pass; the questions it flagged were corrected or left out.

source.name: Web pages cited on each question

items.question: Zoroastrianism's five Gathas, traditionally attributed to Zarathustra himself, contain how many hymns in total?
items.explain: The five Gathas together consist of seventeen hymns, the oldest part of the Avesta.

items.question: The 9th-century Zoroastrian treatise the Dēnkart summarizes the Avesta's books, which are called nasks. How many nasks does it list?
items.explain: Britannica notes that the Dēnkart gives a summary of the Avesta's 21 books, or nasks.

source.title: Zoroastrianism - Ahura Mazda, Dualism, Fire Worship

items.question: Which collection of Zoroastrian prayers and hymns, recited by priests and laypeople in daily worship, is called the 'Small Avesta'?
items.explain: The Khordeh (Khorda) Avesta is the 'Small Avesta', a book of common prayer used in daily worship.

items.question: Which concept, central to the Gathas and Zoroastrian scripture, is compared in one scholarly FAQ to the Dao in Daoism?
items.explain: Asha, usually rendered as truth or cosmic order, is described as a key concept in the Gathas in the way the Dao is in Daoism.

source.title: Zoroastrianism and Avesta: Overview and FAQ

items.question: Within Jain tradition, Mahavira is counted as which Tirthankara of the present era?
items.explain: Mahavira is regarded as the 24th and final Tirthankara of the current cycle.

items.question: In Jainism, what are the five vows called when lay householders observe them in a lesser degree?
items.explain: The five vows are anuvratas (small vows) for lay Jains and mahavratas (great vows) for mendicants.

items.question: Mahavira is said to have reworked the vows of his predecessor Parshvanatha by adding which fifth vow?
items.explain: Mahavira re-established the community on Parshvanatha's teachings and added celibacy as the fifth great vow.

source.title: Tracing the Ancient Roots and Evolution of Jainism • Sociology.Institute

items.question: Which Jain doctrine teaches that truth is many-sided and that no single viewpoint captures all of it?
items.explain: Anekantavada, or non-absolutism, holds that truth can be seen validly from many perspectives at once.

source.title: Understanding Jain Dharma: The Eternal Religion of Ahimsa - Shrimad Rajchandra Mission Dharampur

items.question: At which site in Bihar did Mahavira attain nirvana, making it a major Jain pilgrimage destination?
items.explain: Mahavira preached for about 30 years before attaining nirvana at Pavapuri in Bihar.

source.title: Tracing the Ancient Roots and Evolution of Jainism • Sociology.Institute

items.question: What name is given to the first five Sikhs whom Guru Gobind Singh initiated into the Khalsa in 1699?
items.explain: The Panj Pyare, or 'five beloved ones', were the first Sikhs initiated in the Khalsa's first initiation ceremony.

items.question: Among the Sikh Five Ks, which item is the 'kara'?
items.explain: The five Ks are kesh (uncut hair), kara (steel bracelet), kangha (comb), kirpan (sword) and kachchera (undergarment).

items.question: At which Punjab town did Guru Gobind Singh hold the 1699 assembly at which the first Panj Pyare were initiated?
items.explain: The first five beloved ones were initiated at the historic assembly at Anandpur Sahib in 1699.

items.question: At which of the Sikh Takhts did Guru Gobind Singh historically compile the complete version of the Guru Granth Sahib?
items.explain: Takht Sri Damdama Sahib is historically the place where Guru Gobind Singh compiled the complete Guru Granth Sahib.

items.question: The First Council of Nicaea in 325 met in a city that today is known by what name?
items.explain: Ancient Nicaea is now Iznik, in Turkey.

items.question: Which Greek term, meaning 'of one substance', did the Creed of Nicaea use to affirm the divinity of Christ against Arianism?
items.explain: The council invoked homoousios ('of one substance') to state that the Son is equal to the Father.

items.question: Which young deacon attended the Council of Nicaea as an assistant to Alexander of Alexandria and went on to champion the Nicene Creed against Arianism?
items.explain: Athanasius attended Nicaea as Alexander's assistant and spent much of his life battling Arianism.

items.question: Which council, held in 381, revised the Nicene Creed so that it speaks of the Holy Spirit as worshipped and glorified with the Father and the Son?
items.explain: The 381 revision at Constantinople produced the Niceno-Constantinopolitan Creed, which is often simply called the Nicene Creed.

items.question: Which Latin term, meaning 'and the Son', was added to the Nicene Creed in the West and became a flashpoint in the East-West Schism?
items.explain: The Roman church added 'and the Son' (Filioque) to the creed without consulting the East, which resented it.

items.question: In what year were the mutual excommunications of 1054 between Rome and Constantinople revoked?
items.explain: The excommunications exchanged in 1054 were revoked in 1965.

items.question: Before which Holy Roman Emperor did Martin Luther refuse to recant at the Diet of Worms in 1521?
items.explain: Luther appeared before Charles V at Worms, refused to recant, and was declared a heretic.

items.question: Luther's Ninety-five Theses were launched against the actions of Archbishop Albert and which indulgence preacher?
items.explain: Britannica says Luther launched the Theses against the actions of Albert and Tetzel.

items.question: The 1555 Peace of Augsburg applied which Latin principle, roughly meaning 'whose region, his religion'?
items.explain: The treaty tolerated Lutherans within the Holy Roman Empire on the principle that a ruler's faith set the faith of his territory.

items.question: Bahá'í Ridván commemorates Bahá'u'lláh's 1863 declaration of his mission in a garden near which city, just before he left for Constantinople?
items.explain: Ridván recalls the twelve days Bahá'u'lláh spent in 1863 on the banks of the Tigris in Baghdad, where he declared his mission.

items.question: Which Bahá'í festival, marking the new year at the spring equinox, comes at the end of the nineteen-day fast?
items.explain: The Bahá'í fast takes place in the last month of the year and ends with the festival of Naw-Rúz.

items.question: Which age range of Bahá'ís is expected to observe the sunrise-to-sunset nineteen-day fast, if able?
items.explain: Bahá'ís from age 15 to 70 abstain from food and drink between sunrise and sunset during the fast.

source.title: Baháʼí Holy Days & 19 Day Feast Dates 2026–2027 (Free PDF)

items.question: What is the name of the Shinto ritual in which the buildings of Ise Shrine are rebuilt every 20 years?
items.explain: From the 7th century, Ise's buildings and bridges were reconstructed every 20 years in the ritual called shikinen sengū.

items.question: Izumo-taisha, widely regarded as Japan's oldest major Shinto shrine, is dedicated to which kami, famed as a deity of marriage?
items.explain: Izumo-taisha is dedicated to Ōkuninushi, famous as the Shinto deity of marriage.

items.question: Ise Grand Shrine's tradition of rebuilding every 20 years is traced to the reign of which empress at the end of the 7th century?
items.explain: Since the reign of Empress Jitō, Ise has continued the shikinen sengū tradition of rebuilding on an adjacent site every 20 years.

items.question: The Theravada Pāṭimokkha monastic code consists of how many rules for fully ordained monks (bhikkhus)?
items.explain: The Pāṭimokkha has 227 rules for monks and 311 for nuns; the 348 and 364 figures belong to other nuns' Vinaya traditions.

items.question: Which in-between state after death and before rebirth is especially important in Tibetan Buddhism, and rejected by the Theravada tradition?
items.explain: The bardo is the in-between stage after death and before rebirth. It is central to Tibetan Buddhism; Theravada teaches that rebirth follows death at once.

source.title: Differences Between Theravada and Mahayana Buddhism - buddhanet.net

items.question: Around which century was the Pali Canon followed by Theravada Buddhism first written down?
items.explain: The Pali Canon was first compiled in written form in the first century BCE.

items.question: The Jewish 'Three Weeks' of mourning, which end on Tisha B'Av, begin with which fast day?
items.explain: The three-week period of increasing mourning begins with the fast of the 17th of Tammuz, which recalls the first breach in Jerusalem's walls.

items.question: If the ninth of Av falls on Shabbat, when is the Tisha B'Av fast observed?
answers: Brought forward to the eighth of Av
Postponed until the tenth of Av
items.correct: Postponed until the tenth of Av
items.explain: Tisha B'Av is never observed on Shabbat, so the fast is postponed to the 10th of Av when the 9th falls on a Saturday.

items.question: Which of these Jewish festivals is NOT one of the Three Pilgrimage Festivals?
items.explain: The Three Pilgrimage Festivals are Passover, Shavuot and Sukkot.

items.question: Which rabbinic text, together with the Gemara, makes up the Talmud?
items.explain: The Mishnah combined with the Gemara forms the Talmud.

items.question: In which month of the Islamic calendar does the Hajj take place?
items.explain: Hajj falls from the 8th to the 12th of Dhul Hijjah, the 12th and final month of the Islamic calendar.

items.question: What is the spiritual state of holiness, marked by plain white clothing, that Hajj pilgrims enter?
items.explain: Pilgrims wear plain white clothing and enter a state of holiness known as ihram.

items.question: Which Muslim community rejects the Five Pillars and instead follows a system known as the Four Doors?
items.explain: Alevis are among the Muslim communities that reject the Five Pillars and follow the Four Doors system.

items.question: What is the foundational and central text of the Druze faith?
items.explain: The Epistles of Wisdom (Rasāʾil al-Ḥikma) is the foundational and central text of the Druze faith.

items.question: The Druze faith holds that God took human form in which Fatimid caliph?
items.explain: Hamza ibn Ali, regarded as the founder of the Druze faith, proclaimed that God had become human in the form of al-Hakim bi-Amr Allah.

items.question: Whom do Mandaeans regard as the greatest and final of their prophets?
items.explain: Mandaeans count Adam, Seth, Noah, Shem and John the Baptist as prophets, with John the greatest and final.

items.question: The name 'Mandaean' comes from an Aramaic word, manda, meaning what?
items.explain: Manda means 'knowledge', as does the Greek gnosis, reflecting the Gnostic character of the religion.

items.question: In Rastafari, which biblical name is commonly used for the oppressive and unjust Western society?
items.explain: Rastas associate Babylon with oppressive, unjust society, commonly identified with Western culture.

source.title: Introduction to the Beliefs and Practices of Rastafari

items.question: Sheikh Adi ibn Musafir, the saint whose tomb at Lalish is a focus of Yazidi pilgrimage, was born in the region of which present-day country?
items.explain: Adi ibn Musafir was born around Bait Far in what is now the Beqaa Valley of Lebanon, then settled in Lalish.

items.question: Which Daoist term denotes spontaneity or naturalness and is often paired with wu wei?
items.explain: Daoism emphasizes spontaneity (ziran) and non-action (wu wei), acting in line with the natural course of the universe.

items.question: Which text, honored as a Daoist classic under Emperor Xuanzong of Tang, completes a trilogy with the Daodejing and the Zhuangzi?
items.explain: Emperor Xuanzong designated the Liezi a Daoist classic, completing the trilogy with the Tao Te Ching and Zhuangzi.

items.question: Within which parva (book) of the Mahabharata is the Bhagavad Gita found?
items.explain: The Gita is part of the Mahabharata and sits in the Bhishma Parva chapters 23–40.

items.question: The Prasthanatrayi, the collective foundation of Hindu philosophy, comprises the Upanishads, the Bhagavad Gita and which third text?
items.explain: The Prasthanatrayi is the collective name for the Upanishads, the Bhagavad Gita and the Brahma Sutras.

items.question: The Upanishads are also called Vedanta. What does that term literally mean?
items.explain: Vedanta means 'end of the Vedas' and refers to the Upanishads as the concluding portion of the Vedas.

items.question: Hindu scriptures such as the Vedas, regarded as 'that which is heard', are classed as what?
items.explain: The Vedas and related texts are classed as Shruti, 'that which is heard'.
